text: Every element of America's homeland security plan is critical, because the terrorists are ruthless and resourceful - and we know they are preparing to attack us again.
explanation: Primarily a security threat assessment justifying homeland security measures. 'Ruthless' is a character judgment with moral overtones, which made this borderline, but the sentence's thrust is utilitarian (they 'are preparing to attack us again'), and it makes no appeal to ethical standards, duties, or dignity. I relied on the negative clarification's utilitarian-basis test.

text: o  each minister should prepare and publish a statement of the skills and roles sought for each board.
explanation: Administrative governance rule about ministers publishing skills/roles statements for boards—purely procedural with no normative content.

text: We have had an unprecedented 16 years of continuous economic expansion.
explanation: Descriptive economic claim about 16 years of expansion. Analogous to the negative example on fiscal/growth assessments.

text: We want young New Zealanders to be able to join KiwiSaver and stay in it for their working lives.
explanation: Programmatic statement about KiwiSaver participation. Savings-policy commitment without moral terminology.

text: • It has been four years since the Maori Commercial Settlement Act was passed, and most iwi are yet to receive any form of settlement from the Crown.
explanation: Factually descriptive of settlement delays for iwi. Although the subject (Treaty settlements) is justice-adjacent, the text itself deploys no evaluative or moralized language (e.g., 'unjust,' 'deserve'), so per the codebook it must be coded 0.

text: Those policies have placed the federal government in the driver’s seat,
explanation: Descriptive political observation about federal government being 'in the driver's seat.' No ethical concepts invoked.

text: This has resulted in increased pressure in the health system and failed outcomes for healthcare staff, patients and the public.
explanation: 'Failed outcomes' is a performance evaluation of the health system, not a moral judgment. No appeal to fairness, desert, or dignity—descriptive critique of policy effectiveness.

text: •  More than two in every three New  Zealanders  does unpaid work outside their  own households.
explanation: A statistic about unpaid work. Purely descriptive social data without normative framing.

text: ACARA will work with States and Territories to ensure the Cadetships contribute towards state based senior awards, in the same way as other approved subjects under the National Curriculum
explanation: Administrative education detail about ACARA coordinating cadetships with state awards—procedural, no moral language.

text: That’s why President Obama and Democrats in Congress have enacted infrastructure investments that will
explanation: Programmatic claim about infrastructure investments. Falls under the negative clarification's exclusion of infrastructure/spending descriptions.

text: Increased funding for early childhood education by $550 million, or 40 per cent, since 2008.
explanation: A funding figure for early childhood education—fiscal spending description explicitly excluded by the negative clarification.

text: Labor’s Infrastructure Australia is a secretive organisation.
explanation: Calling Infrastructure Australia 'secretive' is a process/transparency criticism. It does not invoke the codebook's ethical concepts (e.g., corruption, fairness) explicitly; it is a political attack on administrative practice, so coded 0.

text: South Island domestic and industrial users will have their price discounted.
explanation: Technical pricing statement about discounted energy prices for South Island users—economic/administrative content only.

text: Labor has done little to educate the public on the benefits of cleaner fuels.
explanation: Descriptive criticism that Labor has done little public education on cleaner fuels—an assessment of government effort, without moralized terminology.

text: In 1997, a single person on the average industrial wage paid 22% of their income in income tax.
explanation: A tax statistic (22% of income). Purely descriptive fiscal data.

text: Together we're the co-leaders of the Green party
explanation: Self-descriptive statement about being co-leaders of the Green party. No rhetorical or moral content.

text: without allowing emissions from aviation to undermine our goal of a zero-carbon Britain by 2050.
explanation: Frames aviation emissions against a 'zero-carbon Britain by 2050' goal—technical environmental target language without explicit ethical concepts, excluded per the negative clarification on environmental policy.

text: The development of an ‘alternative growth pole’ along the Atlantic Corridor will be pursued.
explanation: Regional development statement about an 'alternative growth pole'—spatial/economic planning language, no moral content.

text: This will be underpinned by new rights for patients.
explanation: 'New rights for patients' frames health-policy guarantees as entitlements, appealing to a rights framework, which the definition includes ('fundamental human rights'). Borderline, since it could be read as legalistic drafting, but the deliberate rights framing is normative terminology going beyond a purely administrative description.

text: Current investment in developing and protecting the Australian farm sector does not recognise the large contribution farmers make to our economy.
explanation: Argues investment fails to 'recognise the large contribution farmers make to our economy.' The contribution invoked is explicitly economic, making this an economic-recognition argument rather than a claim about what farmers morally deserve. Coded 0, though borderline.

text: We recognize that adoption costs can be high and in some cases prohibitive for families.
explanation: Descriptive acknowledgment that adoption costs can be high or prohibitive. No evaluative or moral terminology (e.g., unfair, unjust) is used.

text: We will increase access to the arts for young people, particularly those of disadvantaged backgrounds,
explanation: A programmatic commitment to increase arts access, targeted at 'disadvantaged backgrounds.' Although equity-oriented, 'disadvantaged' functions as a socioeconomic targeting descriptor and no explicit ethical concepts (fairness, justice, desert) are deployed; per the negative clarification, beneficial targeting alone is insufficient.

text: Direct this new spending to health, education, and a few carefully targeted initiatives.
explanation: This is a purely fiscal/spending directive about allocating funds to health and education. Per the negative clarification, descriptions of fiscal spending priorities without explicitly moralized or evaluative language must be coded 0.

text: The Green Party is committed to bringing rail services into public ownership and control.
explanation: A generic programmatic commitment regarding rail ownership structure. It contains no ethical concepts, moral duties, or virtue language, matching the negative clarification's exclusion of generic political commitments.

text: provide direct and meaningful support to land managers in delivering ecoservices; | and
explanation: An administrative statement about supporting land managers in delivering ecoservices. It is technical/environmental policy language without normative moral framing, so it falls under the negative clarification.

text: and providing other services as required, thus contributing to Ireland’s political and economic well being.
explanation: Describes service provision contributing to political and economic well-being. This is utilitarian/economic framing with no appeal to ethical standards, justice, or desert.

text: • Conflicting roles and responsibilities.
explanation: A purely descriptive fragment about conflicting administrative roles. No evaluative or normative terminology is present.

text: An SNP government will strive to ensure that Scotland becomes a world leader in securing a sustainable environment
explanation: An aspirational environmental commitment about Scotland becoming a world leader in sustainability. Per the negative clarification, commitments to positive outcomes like environmental protection without explicitly moralized language are coded 0.

text: With the investment that we are promising in hospital buildings,
explanation: References promised investment in hospital buildings, i.e., infrastructure spending. No ethical or evaluative moral language is used.

text: The question that should still be asked of Labor is:
explanation: A procedural/rhetorical fragment posing a question to an opponent. It contains no ethical concepts, duties, or virtue language.

text: And with new laws to crack down on domestic violence,
explanation: A law-and-order policy commitment to crack down on domestic violence. While the subject is serious, the text uses no explicitly moralized terminology (e.g., justice, dignity, intolerability); it is framed as legislative enforcement and thus falls under the negative clarification.

text: Fine Gael will support the on-going nationwide roll out of the “Food Dudes” Fruit and Vegetable Promotion programme to all primary schools in Ireland.
explanation: A programmatic commitment to roll out a school nutrition programme. Like the negative example on industry training, it details an educational/health policy without moral framing.

text: Every board shall publish before March of each year an annual report on  its own activities as opposed to the wider work of the state body.
explanation: Purely administrative reporting requirements for boards. No normative or ethical content.

text: In particular, as we expand access to talking therapies we expect many more people to recover and be able to seek work again.
explanation: Describes expanded access to talking therapies with a utilitarian rationale (recovery and return to work). No moral duty, desert, or ethical terminology appears.

text: and free up  resources  for whānau development.
explanation: A resource-allocation statement about freeing resources for whānau development. Programmatic and administrative in character, with no moralized language.

text: We will give 1 weeks paid Parental leave for either parent to take, giving them more choice.
explanation: A policy commitment on paid parental leave framed around choice. It proposes a beneficial social policy but does not deploy evaluative moral terminology such as 'deserve' or 'right'.

text: Policy alignment will ensure the wise use of public dollars.
explanation: Concerns fiscal prudence ('wise use of public dollars') and policy alignment. This is administrative/economic framing without appeal to ethical frameworks.

text: At £1.4 Trillion, that equates to £54,353 per household;
explanation: A purely quantitative fiscal statement about debt per household, like the negative example on growth figures. Entirely free of ethical judgment.

text: maintain the Defence Forces’ proud reputation in peacekeeping
explanation: A commitment to maintain the Defence Forces' reputation in peacekeeping. 'Proud reputation' is a reputational/prestige claim rather than an invocation of moral duty, rights, or desert, so it does not meet the threshold for moral rhetoric.

text: The Nationals are determined to eliminate the divide between those living in and those living outside major capital cities, including any limitation on access to a fair legal system that respects the rights and responsibilities of all Australians.
explanation: Explicitly invokes ethical concepts: a 'fair legal system' that 'respects the rights and responsibilities of all Australians', and aims to 'eliminate the divide' between groups. This matches the clarification's markers of fairness, respect, and rights.

text: These moves will eliminate remaining inequality in the income tax system and enhance its progressive nature.
explanation: Explicitly invokes 'inequality' as something to be eliminated and praises the tax system's 'progressive nature'. 'Equality' is listed in the clarification as a key ethical concept, and the statement takes a normative stance against inequality.

text: It is now enshrined in law that we must pay 0.7 per cent of our Gross National Income (GNI) on aid every year.
explanation: Describes a legal requirement to spend 0.7% of GNI on aid. The 'must' denotes statutory obligation rather than moral duty, and the statement is descriptive of fiscal law without ethical framing.

text: Caroline Lucas and housing In July 2014 Caroline Lucas MP introduced a Housing (Affordability, Supply and Tenant Protection) Bill to highlight the problems faced by private tenants.
explanation: A descriptive account of an MP introducing a housing bill. It reports legislative activity without deploying moralized or evaluative language.

text: Support for 2,500 additional aged care beds;
explanation: A spending commitment for aged care beds, purely programmatic. Per the negative clarification, descriptions of fiscal spending on social services without moral framing are coded 0.

text: Develop new community policing structures, through local policing forums in individual communities, to reconnect the Gardaí and local communities in a spirit of genuine partnership.
explanation: Proposes community policing structures and partnership forums. This is an administrative/institutional reform; 'spirit of genuine partnership' is organizational rather than an appeal to ethical duties or virtues.

text: We will: save you money by cutting government waste
explanation: A pledge to save money by cutting government waste. This is economic/efficiency framing; 'waste' here is a fiscal concept, not the ethical concept of corruption.

text: Ireland should be the best place in the world to grow up, and to grow old.
explanation: An aspirational statement that Ireland should be the best place to grow up and grow old. Per the negative clarification, generic aspirational commitments to positive societal outcomes lacking explicitly moralized language (no dignity, desert, justice) are coded 0.

text: Ministerial Cars: We will end the automatic entitlement to a State car for every Government Minister.
explanation: An administrative reform ending ministers' automatic entitlement to state cars. It describes an entitlement rule change without ethical evaluation.

text: If you can’t trust Labour and National to go public about poisoned baby milk then what on earth can you trust them on.
explanation: Invokes 'trust' as the central evaluative standard, accusing opponents of betraying public confidence over poisoned baby milk. Trustworthiness/honesty is a civic virtue, and the rhetorical question morally condemns the opponents' character rather than making a technical argument.

text: All TDs will be entitled to put forward proposals for legislation and a lottery at the start of each session will determine which Bills will be debated.
explanation: Describes a procedural mechanism (lottery for selecting TDs' bills). Purely institutional reform with no moral or evaluative language.

text: We will put in train preparations for the 100th anniversary of the Easter Rising, in a manner that honours the contribution of the men and women of Easter Week,
explanation: States that commemorations will be conducted 'in a manner that honours the contribution of the men and women of Easter Week'. Invoking honour, remembrance, and patriotic sacrifice appeals to civic virtue, matching the clarification's marker of ideals such as patriotism.

text: We will support sensible immigration policies that meet our economic needs
explanation: Supports 'sensible' immigration policies to meet economic needs. This is utilitarian/economic framing without ethical concepts of rights, fairness, or dignity.

text: Establishing the right accountability framework for schools.
explanation: Concerns establishing an accountability framework for schools, where 'right' means appropriate/correct in a technical-administrative sense, not a moral right. No ethical framing.

text: Republicans share President Bush's understanding that just as events in Europe determined the outcome of the Cold War, events in the broader Middle East will set the course for the victory of free nations in the War on Terror.
explanation: Frames geopolitics as the 'victory of free nations', invoking freedom as a fundamental moral-political ideal and casting the conflict in moralized terms of free peoples versus their enemies, rather than in purely strategic or technical terms.

text: • there is appropriate time for debate to be conducted.
explanation: A procedural point about appropriate debate time. Administrative/process language with no moral content.

text: All recreational fishers should help police the system to ensure that there is no room for poachers and quasi ‘recreational’ fishers who sell or raffle their catches.
explanation: Calls on recreational fishers to help enforce rules against poaching. This is regulatory enforcement language; it does not invoke ethical concepts like fairness, rights, or moral duty.

text: •  Created  2000 jobs  during the recession  through state housing upgrades.
explanation: A descriptive claim about jobs created via state housing upgrades. Purely programmatic/economic, akin to the negative infrastructure examples.

text: Constitutional stability for Northern Ireland;
explanation: A generic commitment to constitutional stability for Northern Ireland. No moralized, evaluative, or ethical terminology is present.

text: It will dismantle the dysfunctional Health Service Executive (HSE) that was created by Micheál Martin in 2004,
explanation: Proposes dismantling a 'dysfunctional' health executive. 'Dysfunctional' is a functional/performance critique, not a moral judgment; the text is administrative reform language.

text: conflicts with long-term strategies to cut waste volumes by recycling and reduction, requires huge scale to operate efficiently and generates large volumes of traffic.
explanation: A technical critique of a waste strategy citing scale, efficiency, and traffic. Purely operational/environmental-administrative reasoning without ethical framing.

text: and transition to a prosperous, decarbonized economy.
explanation: Refers to transitioning to a prosperous, decarbonized economy. Economic/environmental framing with no explicit moral terminology.

text: This will support our aim to make Britain the best place in Europe, and one of the top five worldwide, to do business by 2020.
explanation: An economic competitiveness goal (making Britain a top place to do business). Utilitarian framing with no ethical concepts or moral duties.

text: The Nationals believe that, when wealth is generated in a region, a fair share of the resulting government revenue should be returned to that region and to regional Australia more generally.
explanation: Explicitly invokes the ethical concept of fairness: a 'fair share' of government revenue 'should be returned' to regions. This matches the clarification's marker of 'fairness' and a normative claim about what regions are owed.

text: Half a million of us regularly play sport, while 400,000 volunteer as coaches, match officials and referees.
explanation: Descriptive statistics about sports participation and volunteering. No normative or ethical evaluation.

text: We recognise the contribution that Mäori enterprise and entrepreneurship has made to our nation's economy.
explanation: Acknowledges Māori enterprise's contribution to the economy. This is economic recognition framed in utilitarian terms, without invoking rights, justice, or moral desert.

text: We will: Work to secure the full implementation of the Military Covenant in Northern Ireland.
explanation: A commitment to implement the Military Covenant. As written, it is a programmatic pledge to implement a named policy framework and contains no explicitly moralized terminology (no duty, dignity, or desert language), so it falls under the negative clarification.

text: abolish the current 2% limit for funding political parties, which acts against new and smaller parties and could be seen as supporting the status quo;
explanation: Critiques a party-funding cap as disadvantaging new parties and entrenching the status quo. While it hints at inequity, it uses no explicit ethical terminology (fairness, justice, rights); it is framed as a descriptive institutional critique.

text: After so long in office, Mr Howard has forgotten what fairness actually means.
explanation: Explicitly invokes the ethical concept of 'fairness', accusing Mr Howard of forgetting what it means. This directly matches the clarification's marker of ethical concepts such as fairness, delivering a moral condemnation rather than a technical critique.

text: • develop Parents as First Teacher (PAFT) programmes across the country.
explanation: A programmatic commitment to develop parenting education programmes. Like the negative example on apprenticeships, it details an educational policy without moral virtues or duties.

text: We will crackdown on overseas producers who don’t cooperate with anti-dumping investigations
explanation: A trade-enforcement pledge against producers not cooperating with anti-dumping investigations. Regulatory/economic framing with no ethical or moralized language.

text: Labour will ensure that the Defence  Forces are appropriately equipped and staffed to meet Ireland’s  obligations to United Nations and EU peacekeeping missions.
explanation: Commits to equipping Defence Forces to meet international 'obligations' to UN/EU peacekeeping missions. The obligations referenced are institutional/legal, and the language is administrative rather than an appeal to moral duty or humanitarian ethics.

text: Processing of applications and decision-making is subject to long delays, while the absence of legislation means there is frequent resort to the Courts for judicial review.
explanation: Describes administrative delays and litigation over application processing. A descriptive critique of bureaucratic functioning without moral or evaluative ethical language.
